Inter fusion (R3) vs R1: −0.005 [−0.064, +0.055], p 0.98. With package features the early-fusion gain is not significant (+0.055 [−0.002, +0.105], adjusted p 0.092).
2: **Scanner dominates the image-based representations, then patient.** A probe identifies the scanner perfectly from R0–R3 (AUROC 1.000), against 0.55 from CNV alone. A sample's nearest held-out neighbour is from the same patient 62–84% of the time (93% for CNV), against 16% by chance. Progression (0.84–0.91), grade (0.81–0.87) and tile count (0.71–0.79) come next, and the image alone does not encode CNV complexity (0.48). Scanner is not confounded with progression: 28% of samples are from progressors on either scanner (descriptive, not pre-specified).
